speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a neck swelling; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me how long you have had this lump and if it has been growing?

Also, has the swelling changed in size when you swallow, and do you have any symptoms like fever, difficulty breathing, or voice changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Cervical Lymphadenopathy) secondary to Head and Neck primary or unknown primary.

Given your history of colon cancer and the specific location and nature of this painless, growing nape swelling, I need to confirm if this is a recurrence or a new metastasis. Can you specify if you have had any previous radiation therapy to your head, neck, or chest, and do you notice any lumps under your jaw or in your armpits?

REQUEST TEST: Neck Ultrasound with Doppler, CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis, and FNA (Fine Needle Aspiration) of the nape swelling.

REQUEST IMAGES: Neck US, CT Chest/Abd/Pelvis.
